title: Opening and McBee's nighttime routine with his bass
summary: Rowe opens the second session; McBee describes his late hours and checking in with his bass each day.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m pleased to have a second session with Cecil McBee about two weeks after our first conversation. Thanks for finding time again. And you mentioned that you still live, your bio clock, you’re still a nighttime person, is that correct?

Oh yeah. You know when you’re in Tokyo, which is 14 hours in advance of your clock, for a couple of weeks and then you return to New York, supposedly back in reverse to what your rhythm would be about. And then you go to California. And then to Texas. So over all these years I managed to function around this time of the day Eastern Time. I’m up about maybe 11, 11:30.
And the first thing I do is run to my bass and make sure that I’m okay. Really. I do.

Yeah, that’s my standard for the day. I’ll play a couple of notes because there’s things that I’m working on now that I’ve had a favor to over the years, things are opening up now on the instrument that, you know, that I’m very excited about. So in a way it’s cyclic.
